questions.text: My editor keeps warning "Found GraphQL documents in tagged templates, but GraphQLSP is configured to search for graphql()/gql() calls." Where is that produced, and which setting makes it go away?
questions.how_found: Read packages/graphqlsp/src/index.ts to see getGraphQLDiagnostics wired into proxy.getSemanticDiagnostics, then read diagnostics.ts. getModeMismatchDiagnostic (169-215) first does a cheap regex probe of the file text for any of the `templates` names followed by a backtick or paren, then emits a Warning under MODE_MISMATCH_CODE (52007, declared at line 60) telling you to set "templateIsCallExpression": false in the tsconfig plugin entry.
questions.rg_query: Found GraphQL documents in tagged templates
questions.why_asked: A warning with an unfamiliar code showed up on day one on an existing project; I need to know whether it's a real problem and which config knob it refers to.

questions.text: If a source pushes some values asynchronously, does toArray still collect them?
questions.how_found: Read src/sinks.ts. toArray subscribes, pulls after every push, and returns as soon as the synchronous recursion unwinds; anything emitted later is dropped and a Close talkback is sent before returning (`if (!ended) talkback(TalkbackKind.Close)`, line 214). The doc block at 182-198 states this explicitly.
questions.why_asked: I saw toArray used in a test helper and want to know if it's safe on a source that involves a promise or timer, or whether I should use toPromise/toAsyncIterable instead.

questions.text: For server-side rendering we call toStatic() — what exactly comes back, and what does calling it do to the internal queues?
questions.how_found: src/index.ts line 13 re-exports `dispatcher.toStatic`. The implementation in src/dispatcher/index.ts returns { lang, title, links, scripts, metas }, applies the title template to the LAST entry of each queue (not the first, unlike the browser path), dedupes metas after reversing the queue, HTML-escapes meta content, stamps every link with data-hoofd="1", and then empties every queue and resets the indices so the next request starts clean.
questions.why_asked: I'm adding SSR to a route and need to know whether toStatic is idempotent or destructive — getting that wrong leaks head tags between requests.

questions.text: Our generated turbo cache file has a `/** @gql.tada/hash sha256:... */` comment above every entry. What reads those, and can I strip them?
questions.how_found: cache.ts declares HASH_COMMENT = /@gql\.tada\/hash\s+([^\s*]+)/ (line 4). readCachedTurboDocuments parses the previous output with the TS parser, walks the `setupCache` interface, and for each member reads the last leading comment matching that regex (getHashComment, 57-65). Entries without a recoverable hash are skipped, so removing the comments forces a full re-typecheck. The comments are written back out in commands/turbo/runner.ts line 261.
questions.why_asked: The generated file is checked in and the comments look like noise in review diffs; before deleting them I need to know whether they're load-bearing.

questions.text: Upstream keeps its constant lookup maps immutable at load-time, but in our slimmed build they come out mutable. Which step in the pipeline strips that, and why?
questions.how_found: Walked scripts/rollup/config.mjs to the babel plugins it registers, then read scripts/babel/*.mjs. transformObjectFreeze.mjs is a Babel visitor that matches any CallExpression whose callee is the member expression Object.freeze and replaces the whole call with its first argument, so the wrapper disappears from the bundle entirely. Sibling transforms in the same folder do the same for dev assertions and for computed Symbol.toStringTag getters.
questions.why_asked: Code that relies on upstream's runtime immutability will silently behave differently once this package is aliased in; I want to know exactly what our build changes about semantics, not just about size.

questions.text: Do the two upstream helpers that compare an earlier and a later API surface still do any real work here, or are they hollow placeholders kept just so imports keep resolving?
questions.how_found: Listed the alias/ tree (it mirrors the upstream package's folder layout) and read alias/utilities/findBreakingChanges.mjs. Both exported functions take underscore-prefixed, unused parameters and unconditionally `return []`. Only the two enum-like constant objects above them are real, so anything importing them compiles and runs but always sees an empty result.
questions.why_asked: A CI job of ours diffs two versions of the API and reports nothing since we aliased this package; I need to know whether that's a bug on our side or a deliberate stub.

questions.text: Out of the box, which two tag names are treated as marking an inline query, and how do I register an extra name?
questions.how_found: Followed isGraphQLFunctionIdentifier in packages/graphqlsp/src/ast/checks.ts line 17 back to the set it consults, which is the single line of ast/templates.ts: `new Set(['gql', 'graphql'])`. The set is mutable and packages/graphqlsp/src/index.ts line 70 adds the `template` value from the tsconfig plugin entry to it at startup, which is the supported way to add a third name.
questions.why_asked: Our codebase wraps documents in a custom-named helper and the editor tooling ignores them; I need to know whether that name has to be registered somewhere.

questions.text: In the mini grammar, how does a repetition marker bind to whatever comes before it, and what happens if it appears with nothing preceding it?
questions.how_found: Read src/parser.js, the single-pass character scanner over the template's quasis. The `?`, `+` and `*` branch only fires when the assignment `lastMatch = currentSequence[currentSequence.length - 1]` yields a truthy previous entry; it then mutates that entry in place rather than creating a node of its own. With an empty current sequence the branch's guard fails and control falls through to the final `else`, which calls syntaxError(char) and throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token "?"`.
questions.why_asked: I mistyped a rule and got an opaque SyntaxError with no position; understanding where these markers attach tells me how to read the error and how the generated matcher will backtrack.

questions.text: Why does our troubleshooting walkthrough pause noticeably between stages on a laptop, yet feel instant on build agents? Is the pause intentional?
questions.how_found: Read packages/cli-utils/src/commands/doctor/runner.ts. A local `delay = (ms = 700)` helper is awaited between every yielded status line; it short-circuits to Promise.resolve() when process.env.CI is set, and otherwise resolves via setTimeout. The comment above it says the tasks complete too quickly and are slowed down on purpose so the output is readable.
questions.why_asked: It looked like our own project was making the tool slow, and I was about to profile it — knowing it's cosmetic pacing saves a wasted afternoon and tells me not to copy the pattern into new commands.

questions.text: Two components on the same screen declare competing wording for the tab label — why does the deeper declaration win, and what happens if it disappears?
questions.how_found: Read src/hooks/useTitle.ts, which just forwards to the dispatcher, then src/dispatcher/index.ts. Additions are spliced in at an index that increments within a batch rather than being appended, so the deeper hook's entry lands in front; the whole batch is then flushed once per frame (setTimeout of 1000/60) and only the head of the queue is applied. Removal splices the entry out and, when it was at position 0, immediately re-applies the next entry — so the shallower declaration comes back as a fallback instead of leaving the previous wording stuck.
questions.why_asked: Our layout sets one value and the route sets another, and I need to know which one is authoritative and whether navigating away restores the outer one or leaves a stale value.

questions.text: We wrote "tadaOutputLocation": "${configDir}/graphql-env.d.ts" in the tsconfig plugin entry. Which code actually expands ${configDir}, and what happens if I typo the placeholder name?
questions.how_found: The natural first stop is GraphQLSP, since the placeholder is written in its tsconfig entry — but GraphQLSP/packages/graphqlsp/src/graphql/getSchema.ts only calls parseConfig imported from @gql.tada/internal. That package lives in the gql.tada repo: packages/internal/src/config.ts, where parseSchemaConfig's resolveConfigDir runs `input.replace(/\${([^}]+)}/, ...)` against the three tada*Location options, substituting rootPath for `configDir` and throwing a TadaError ("did you mean 'configDir'?") for any other name. Note the regex is un-flagged, so only the first occurrence in a path is replaced.
questions.why_asked: The expansion is written in GraphQLSP's config but implemented in another repo; I need to know which options support it, and whether a misspelling fails loudly or silently produces a nonsense path.

questions.text: The CLI exposes one keypress stream that several places subscribe to — does each subscriber add another raw-mode listener on stdin, or is there a single underlying subscription?
questions.how_found: gql.tada/packages/cli-utils/src/term/tty.ts builds inputSource as pipe(fromReadStream(process.stdin, ...), onStart, onEnd, share) and derives cancelSource from it with another share — so the guarantee is entirely `share`'s, which lives in the wonka repo. wonka/src/operators.ts share keeps a sinks array and only calls the input source when `sinks.length === 1`; every later sink is fanned out from that one subscription, and the upstream Close is only sent once the last sink has detached. So setRawMode/emitKeypressEvents run once, not per subscriber.
questions.why_asked: Two commands read the same input stream and I need to know whether adding a third consumer risks double-handling Ctrl-C or leaving the terminal in raw mode.
